lesson.summary: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations
points: A declaration pairs a type and name; initialization supplies a first value, and assignment changes it.
Practice int, float, double and char, with suitable printf formats.
Names are case sensitive. Do not read an uninitialized automatic local.
lesson.title: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations

game.objective: Declare float: declare resource as float, apply resource + 15.5, and print each result with %.1f. Dataset 2 starts with [-15, 0, 15, 15]. Match every stream. Use a full main function and a return statement.
game.hint: Declare before use. float resource = readInput(); creates the named game-port value; printf uses %.1f.
game.controls: Edit the C program. Run tests all streams; Step shows declarations, assignments and output. readInput() is a LogiCade game-port helper declared in logicade.h. This safe practice runtime supports a documented C subset.

source_spec.game_concept: A logic puzzle set in Eldritch Ruins – Rune Circle, a circle of glowing runes: the ruin warden must handle echo phantoms while practicing lists. Core idea – Comprehension Lab: Build new lists in one line with list comprehensions to transform ancient keys.
source_spec.theme: Eldritch Ruins – Rune Circle: a circle of glowing runes
source_spec.core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
source_spec.player_objective: Declare float: declare resource as float, apply resource + 15.5, and print each result with %.1f. Dataset 2 starts with [-15, 0, 15, 15]. Match every stream. Use a full main function and a return statement.

source_spec.win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
source_spec.lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
